sampling_model.design: Deterministic oracle identification from the observational MAG signature and \(K\) intervention-regime MAG signatures generated by one common basal selected DAG.
sampling_model.units: The primitive object is a fully specified member \(\eta\in\mathfrak M_{D,K}^{\mathrm{Dai}}\). At \(K=0\), its only oracle law is \(P_{\eta}^{(0)}=\mathcal L_{\eta}(X\mid S^*=\mathbf 1)\); at \(K\ge 1\), each comparison additionally uses \(P_{\eta,k}^{\mathrm{pool}}\) on \(X\cup\{\zeta_k\}\).
sampling_model.treatment: Regime membership is observed, while every direct soft-intervention target set \(T_k(\eta)\) is latent and may differ from the indicator-neighbor set \(Z_k\).
sampling_model.overlap: The common pre-treatment selection event has positive probability, so every selected oracle law is well defined.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Not applicable; the proposal begins from exact regime-MAG adjacency and unshielded-collider inputs.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 3 proves CDIS soundness, while p. 8, lines 652--661, says completeness remains uncertain and is conjectured.
Sections 3--4 establish arrowhead and tail completeness for the observational PAG rules, with Theorem 2 providing the representative-MAG construction.
Two maximal ancestral graphs are Markov equivalent if and only if they have the same adjacencies and colliders with order.
The public abstract, lines 5--9, describes a known-target enumeration-based completion that is sound and theoretically complete; official theorem text was inaccessible.
We present the first polynomial-delay MAG listing method.
We provide a complete characterization of the equivalence class under soft interventions with unknown targets.
We develop a provably sound and complete algorithm, F-FCI, using both observational and interventional data.

body.tldr: Selection before perturbation couples every regime-specific MAG through one common basal selected DAG, so completing the regimes independently can miss endpoints compelled by their joint origin. The deterministic kernel is a fixed finite within-regime and cross-regime rule calculus whose monotone closure equals the canonical observed-endpoint SI-PAG for Dai et al.'s causally sufficient, unknown-target twin-graph class. A graph replacement lemma and a simultaneous faithful-kernel realization lemma yield an exact frontier for intervention-created selected--selected endpoints conditional on the ancestral selected set. The open mathematical step lifts these witnesses through unknown selection membership and a common exterior completion, producing opposing common-basal realizations for every endpoint left circular. If the fixed rules have uniformly polynomial matchers, monotone saturation uses only polynomially many strict endpoint updates.

project_justification.gap: Dai et al., Theorem 3 and p. 8, lines 646--662, prove CDIS soundness and explicitly leave completeness uncertain because complete rules for their Lemma 6 background knowledge are unavailable. Their Lemmas 4--6 on pp. 6--7 supply the fixed-model semantic inputs but not opposing common-basal representatives. Zhang, Sections 3--4 and Theorem 2, proves arrowhead and tail completeness for one observational PAG without joint regime realizability. The Zhou--Kocaoglu author listing at lines 27--31 and public abstract at lines 5--9 describe an enumeration-based completion in a known-target setting; official theorem numbering and text were inaccessible, so no formula-level claim is used.
project_justification.niche: The missing object is a dimension- and regime-count-independent endpoint calculus for unknown-target interventions after common pre-treatment selection, together with a semantic guarantee that every residual circle is genuine common-basal ambiguity.
project_justification.fill: The project combines full regime-MAG adjacency and unshielded-collider signatures with observable selectedness certificates, signature-monotone path propagation, graph replacement, and simultaneous faithful-kernel realization. It proves the fixed-\(A(\eta)\) endpoint frontier, solves the unknown-selection lifting problem, derives a complete fixed local calculus, and obtains conditional polynomial saturation without enumerating compatible basal DAGs.

body.related_work: Dai et al., Lemmas 4--6 on pp. 6--7, characterize intervention-created observed adjacencies, indicator neighbors, and endpoint semantics in the destination pre-treatment-selection twin class. Their Theorem 3 and the explicit discussion on p. 8, lines 646--662, prove CDIS soundness and leave completeness uncertain because complete orientation rules for the Lemma 6 background knowledge are not known. Zhang's primary article separates arrowhead and tail completeness in Sections 3--4; its Theorem 2 constructs a representative MAG and completes one observational PAG, but does not synchronize several intervention projections through one basal selected DAG. Ali, Richardson, and Spirtes characterize equivalence of a single MAG through adjacencies and ordered colliders; those invariants guide the replacement lemma but do not enforce a common basal fiber. The Zhou--Kocaoglu author publication listing, entry 2 at lines 27--31, verifies Zihan Zhou and Murat Kocaoglu, the title, ICML 2026, and the venue. Its public abstract record, paper 1 at lines 5--9, says that known-target interventional FCI can be incomplete, describes a complete compatible-MAG enumeration, and describes extra local rules only as a tightening. The official OpenReview theorem numbering and text were inaccessible, so this proposal makes no formula-level claim about that paper. Wang, Du, and Zhou give polynomial-delay MAG listing and locally complete propagation under singleton background knowledge; their work informs only the conditional saturation accounting, while selectedness here is derived from the multi-regime oracle signature. Jaber et al., p. 2 and Theorem 3 on p. 7, assume no selection bias and prove completeness for their unknown-target soft-intervention equivalence class, so they do not cover pre-treatment twin coupling. Luo et al.'s public ICLR 2026 record describes F-FCI for latent confounding with post-treatment selection; that timing and fine-grained interventional fiber are distinct from the causally sufficient common-basal pre-treatment-selected class here.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The fixed-\(A(\eta)\) replacement theorem does not solve the headline problem. \(\operatorname{RepGraph}(\eta,B)\) is a graphical specification, and preservation of skeletons and unshielded colliders alone does not make \(\operatorname{Real}(\eta,B)\) nonempty; that requires a joint faithful-kernel realization. Beyond fixed \(A(\eta)\), selection membership may vary over \(\mathcal C(\mathcal O)\), a single exterior DAG completion must serve every regime, and \(Z_k\) identifies a union of direct targets and indirectly affected ancestrally selected vertices. A proof that sets \(T_k(\eta)=Z_k\), guesses \(A(\eta)\), completes regimes independently, or invokes a global basal-DAG enumerator does not establish \(\mathrm{oeq:selection\mbox{-}lifting}\).
body.honest_scope: The graph replacement, simultaneous faithful-kernel realization, combined replacement theorem, and intervention-created-edge frontier conditional on \(A(\eta)\) are theorem candidates and remain to be proved for the complete regime signatures. The retained-edge sanity reduction records why basal adjacencies lie outside that frontier. The full finite rule list, unknown-selection-membership lift, common exterior completion, separation of direct targets from indirectly affected selected vertices, and residual-circle witnesses are open and central. The complete-calculus theorem is deliberately downstream of \(\mathrm{oeq:selection\mbox{-}lifting}\). At \(K=0\), the sole selected law is \(P_{\eta}^{(0)}=\mathcal L_{\eta}(X\mid S^*=\mathbf 1)\), with no \(k\) or \(\zeta_k\); the Dai observational image is contained in the unrestricted observational MAG fiber, so every Zhang-compelled endpoint remains compelled, but equality of the fibers is not claimed. For \(K\ge 1\), each intervention comparison uses its binary-indicator pooled law on \(X\cup\{\zeta_k\}\). The proposal excludes latent basal common causes, post-treatment selection, regime-specific selection mechanisms, and global basal-DAG enumeration as the headline method.
